pattern.crimePattern: fake land agent kills a buyer who discovered the title was not his to sell; a friend gives him an alibi
pattern.notes: Fictional block, fictional parcel number. Fake plot sales on the city's edge are a widely reported pattern; no real case or company is depicted.

ob.reportedBy: Saida Abdallah, resident, flat C-11-03, Tumaini Towers, Pipeline
ob.text: Saida Abdallah, resident of Tumaini Towers, Embakasi Pipeline, reports that her neighbour, Pauline Kanana (43), a primary-school teacher, was found dead in flat C-11-04, eleventh floor, at 22:35. The door was ajar.

people.name: Pauline Kanana
people.bio: Saved for eleven years to buy a plot in Kitengela. Paid KSh 650,000 for it in March.

image.brief: Kenyan woman, early 40s, short natural hair, small gold stud earrings, a teacher's lanyard, a red marking pen clipped to her blouse, calm and determined, ID-photo framing

people.name: Evans Nyakundi
people.bio: Sells plots on the city's edge from a folder of agreements. Sold Pauline the Kitengela plot.

image.brief: Kenyan man, mid 50s, grey suit slightly too big, a leather document folder under his arm, gold-rimmed glasses, a salesman's smile, ID-photo framing

people.name: Philip Masinde
people.bio: Has known Evans since school. Says Evans spent the whole evening in his flat.

image.brief: Kenyan man, early 50s, round face, a cardigan over a vest, slippers, a television remote still in his hand, uneasy, ID-photo framing

people.name: Martin Sang
people.bio: Separated from Pauline for six years. They have been arguing over their son's school fees.

image.brief: Kenyan man, late 40s, cargo-terminal hi-vis vest over a jumper, an ID badge on a lanyard, tired eyes, ID-photo framing

people.name: Saida Abdallah
people.bio: Lives through the wall from Pauline. Found her.

image.brief: Kenyan woman, mid 30s, a pale blue hijab, a long cardigan, a set of keys in her hand, shocked, ID-photo framing

people.name: Julius Mwaniki
people.bio: Runs the one compound gate: gate book, laminated visitor badges, a torch.

image.brief: Kenyan man, early 60s, a navy security jumper with plain shoulder patches, a torch clipped to his belt, grey stubble, conscientious, ID-photo framing

locations.name: Flat C-11-04, Tumaini Towers, Pipeline
locations.description: Eleven floors up, no lift. A tidy two-bedroom flat: a sofa with lace covers, exercise books stacked for marking, a charcoal iron on its trivet by the ironing board. A document folder lies open on the table.

hotspots.label: Living room
hotspots.text: Pauline lies by the ironing board. Her heavy charcoal iron is on the floor beside her.

hotspots.label: Table
hotspots.text: A carbon copy of a handwritten letter, signed by Pauline, on top of her marking.

hotspots.label: Document folder
hotspots.text: Her document folder, open: a sale agreement for a plot.

hotspots.label: Under the agreement
hotspots.text: An official land search result, folded behind the agreement.

hotspots.label: Under the sofa
hotspots.text: Something flat and laminated has slid under the sofa's lace skirt.

hotspots.label: Door of C-11-03
hotspots.text: Saida Abdallah stands in her own doorway, the security chain still hanging loose.

hotspots.label: Window
hotspots.text: Three towers, twelve storeys each. From here the gate yard is a small lit square far below.

image.brief: a tidy eleventh-floor flat in a Nairobi high-rise estate at night, a sofa with lace covers, stacks of school exercise books, an old charcoal iron on a trivet beside an ironing board, an open document folder on a table, city lights and two other tower blocks through the window, no people in focus

locations.name: Compound gate, Tumaini Towers
locations.description: One steel gate for three towers. A guard hut, a gate book on a chain, a board of numbered laminated visitor badges on hooks. Hook 14 is empty.

hotspots.label: Gate book
hotspots.text: Every visitor signs in, says which flat, and takes a badge. They hand it back on the way out.

hotspots.label: Guard hut
hotspots.text: Julius Mwaniki is already holding the gate book open at tonight's page.

image.brief: the steel gate of a high-rise housing compound in Nairobi at night, a guard hut, a gate book on a chain, a pegboard of numbered laminated visitor badges with one hook empty, three tall residential towers behind

evidence.title: The body in the living room

body.note: Report language only. Struck with her own heavy charcoal iron.

image.brief: a living room floor beside an ironing board, an old heavy charcoal iron lying on its side on the tiles, a toppled pile of exercise books, no body visible

body.text: Mr Evans Nyakundi: refund my KSh 650,000 by Friday or I report you to the police. A copy of my search goes with this letter. — P. Kanana

body.result: Parcel registered to a different person. No transfer to E. Nyakundi on record.

body.text: TUMAINI TOWERS — VISITOR — RETURN AT GATE

facts.text: Saida Abdallah found her neighbour Pauline Kanana dead in flat C-11-04 at 22:35. The door was ajar.
Pauline was struck with her own heavy charcoal iron.
Pauline's letter, copy: 'Mr Evans Nyakundi: refund my KSh 650,000 by Friday or I report you to the police.'
Sale agreement: a Kitengela plot for KSh 650,000, Evans Nyakundi signing as vendor.
In the corner of the agreement, an oval rubber-stamp impression: 'Title search — certified — REGISTRAR OF TITLES'.
Pauline's own official search: the parcel is registered to a different person entirely. Evans never owned it.
Laminated visitor badge No. 14 was lying under Pauline's sofa.
Saida: Pauline came up the stairs with her shopping at 20:05.
Saida: from about 20:15 she heard voices through the wall: Pauline's and a man's.
Saida: at about 20:45 there was a crash, then quiet. At 22:35 she saw the door ajar and found Pauline.
Saida stayed in her own flat with the security chain on until she looked out at 22:35.
Saida: last week Pauline's ex-husband, Martin, shouted at her on the stairs about their son's school fees.
Gate book: '20:10 — Evans N. — visiting C-11-04 — badge 14.' The return column is blank. At 22:00: 'Badge 14 NOT RETURNED.'
Julius: a delivery van blocked the gate at about 20:55. While he moved it on, he didn't see who went out.
Julius: from Tower A, the only way to Tower C is across the yard in front of his hut. Until the van came at 20:55, nobody from A crossed it, Philip included.
Julius was at the gate from 18:00; residents and the van driver saw him there all evening.
Martin's clock card, cargo terminal, JKIA: in 18:52, out 07:04.
Philip: "Evans was with me in my flat, A-3-02, from seven until ten. We watched the news and the football."
Philip admits he fell asleep after the seven o'clock news. When he woke up, Evans was there and asked him to say he'd been there all evening.
Evans: "Ask Philip where I was."
Evans: "That plot is clean. She was confused."
Martin: "I was at work all night."
Martin: he and Pauline argued about the fees, "but I would never touch her. She is my son's mother."

interrogations.intro: Evans sits with his folder on his knees and his hands flat on top of it. "I am a businessman. I have nothing to say."

topics.reply: Searches go wrong. Clerks make mistakes. Land is complicated.
Every paper is stamped. Certified. Look at it.
Badges. Everyone has badges in this place.

interrogations.intro: Philip opens the door of A-3-02 in his slippers, the television still on behind him. "Evans? Yes, he was here. All evening."

topics.reply: We were at school together in Kakamega. He sells plots. He does well.

interrogations.intro: Martin takes the call on his break at the cargo terminal. A forklift reverses behind him. "Pauline? Pauline?"

topics.reply: We argued about the fees. Shouted, even. But I would never touch her. She is my son's mother.

interrogations.intro: Saida holds the end of her door chain as if it were still fastened. "I heard it all through that wall. I just didn't know what I was hearing."

topics.reply: A man in a grey suit came to see her last month with papers. She was so happy that day. "My plot," she said.

interrogations.intro: Julius taps the empty hook on his badge board. "Fourteen. Every badge comes back. Every one. Except tonight."

topics.reply: He signed in at ten past eight for C-11-04. Polite. A suit. I gave him fourteen.
Mzee Philip in Tower A? To get to Tower C you cross my yard. Nobody from A crossed it before that van came. After that, I was busy shouting at a driver.

contradictions.reaction: ...I fell asleep after the seven o'clock news. When I woke up he was there, sweating, on my sofa. He asked me to say he had been there the whole time. I didn't ask why. I didn't want to know why.

prosecutor.pass: A friend's alibi that fell asleep, a gate book that didn't, and badge fourteen under her sofa. That will hold.
fail: Doesn't hold up. A man who lies for a friend has a friend. Who did he lie for?
No. The ex-husband was clocked in at the airport. Follow the badge.

proof.concludes: Philip said Evans was in A-3-02 from seven, but Evans signed in at the gate at 20:10 to visit C-11-04. Pressed, Philip admits he was asleep and Evans asked him to lie.
Pauline was alive at 20:05. A man was with her from about 20:15, and the crash came at 20:45: inside Evans's visit.
The badge issued to Evans at 20:10, never returned, is under her sofa. She had found out his plot was not his to sell. Evans Nyakundi killed Pauline.

eliminations.why: Nobody from Tower A crossed the gate yard, the only way to Tower C, before 20:55; the crash was at 20:45.
Martin was clocked in at the JKIA cargo terminal from 18:52 to 07:04.
Saida stayed in her own flat with the chain on; she is the one whose timings fix the window.
Julius was at the gate all evening, seen by residents and the van driver.

reconstruction.text: March. Pauline pays Evans KSh 650,000 for a plot in Kitengela. The agreement carries a certified stamp from the registrar.
June. A friend at the lands office runs a real search. The plot belongs to someone else. On Monday she writes to Evans: refund by Friday, or the police.
20:10. Evans signs in at the gate for C-11-04 and takes badge 14. He climbs eleven floors.
He tries to talk her round. She tells him the police already have a copy. At 20:45 he picks up the iron.
20:55. A delivery van blocks the gate and the guard steps out to move it. Evans crosses the yard to Tower A unseen. Badge 14 stays under her sofa. He wakes his old friend: "Say I was here."

tier1.line: Philip says his friend was in Tower A all evening. The gate keeps its own book. Read it.

tier2.line: Badge 14 went out at the gate at 20:10 and never came back. Where did it end up?

glossary.def: Respectful word for an older man.

ui.beatNotes: Linked claims: when Philip's alibi breaks, Evans's whereabouts ("Ask Philip where I was"), which depended on it, turn grey in the notebook automatically. The player sees one broken claim knock out another.
